evidence.note: Repeated TodoWrite updates across the run — a maintained checklist of task families/state rather than a one-time plan.
Ran the aggregate score multiple times at intervals as edits landed, allowing comparison of the pass rate over time.
Filtered output to only files with failures / remaining failures, focusing attention on what's left rather than re-checking already-green files.
Ended by pulling per-file MVP and per-file SIMD scores — a per-file pass/fail ledger of done-vs-remaining.
Consistent edit→rebuild→re-test→re-aggregate cycles, tying edits back to score movement.

reasoning: The agent keeps a live checklist (recurring TodoWrite) and repeatedly measures both the aggregate score and per-file failures as work proceeds, filtering to remaining failures rather than polishing green areas — clearly above the level-5 'usable checklist / rough tracking' anchor. It approaches level 8's precise per-file ledger and score-trend tracking, but there is no explicit regression-catch or stall-detection evidence, and the condensed/truncated trajectory does not demonstrate sustained monitoring across the full SIMD horizon, so it falls short of 8. A 6 reflects solid, ongoing but not fully self-correcting progress tracking.
